+describe('Request ID Middleware with trustIncoming', () => {
+  function generateWord() {
+    return 'HonoIsWebFramework'
+  }
+
+  const app = new Hono()
+  app.use('/trusted', requestId({ generator: generateWord }))
+  app.use('/untrusted', requestId({ generator: generateWord, trustIncoming: false }))
+  app.get('/trusted', (c) => c.text(c.get('requestId') ?? 'No Request ID'))
+  app.get('/untrusted', (c) => c.text(c.get('requestId') ?? 'No Request ID'))
+
+  it('Should use incoming request id header by default', async () => {
+    const res = await app.request('http://localhost/trusted', {
+      headers: {
+        'X-Request-Id': 'hono-is-hot',
+      },
+    })
+    expect(res).not.toBeNull()
+    expect(res.status).toBe(200)
+    expect(res.headers.get('X-Request-Id')).toBe('hono-is-hot')
+    expect(await res.text()).toBe('hono-is-hot')
+  })
+
+  it('Should use incoming request id header when trustIncoming is true', async () => {
+    const trustedApp = new Hono()
+    trustedApp.use('*', requestId({ generator: generateWord, trustIncoming: true }))
+    trustedApp.get('/requestId', (c) => c.text(c.get('requestId') ?? 'No Request ID'))
+
+    const res = await trustedApp.request('http://localhost/requestId', {
+      headers: {
+        'X-Request-Id': 'hono-is-hot',
+      },
+    })
+    expect(res).not.toBeNull()
+    expect(res.status).toBe(200)
+    expect(res.headers.get('X-Request-Id')).toBe('hono-is-hot')
+    expect(await res.text()).toBe('hono-is-hot')
+  })
+
+  it('Should ignore incoming request id header when trustIncoming is false', async () => {
+    const res = await app.request('http://localhost/untrusted', {
+      headers: {
+        'X-Request-Id': 'hono-is-hot',
+      },
+    })

Done. The option is implemented and tests pass.

## Changes

**`src/middleware/request-id/request-id.ts`**
- Added `trustIncoming?: boolean` to `RequestIdOptions` (`request-id.ts:17`).
- Destructured with `trustIncoming = true` so default behavior is unchanged (`request-id.ts:47`).
- Gate the incoming header read: `let reqId = trustIncoming && headerName ? c.req.header(headerName) : undefined` (`request-id.ts:50`). When `false`, the header is ignored and `reqId` falls through to `generator(c)`, which is still set via `c.set('requestId', reqId)` and returned in the response header (`request-id.ts:55-59`).
- Added JSDoc for the new option (`request-id.ts:27`).

**`src/middleware/request-id/index.test.ts`**
- New `describe('Request ID Middleware with trustIncoming')` block covering:
  - Default (implicit `true`) trusts an incoming valid header.
  - Explicit `trustIncoming: true` trusts the header.
  - `trustIncoming: false` ignores a valid incoming header and uses the generator.
  - `trustIncoming: false` without a header still uses the generator.
  - Generated value is surfaced through both the response body (`c.get('requestId')`) and the response header.
